title: Even-n limit ρ→1 is only conditional (RM weight-enumerator input unproved)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: In Theorem `thm:asy`(1) and eq. `eq:cited`, the limit $\rho(n)\to1$ for even $n$ is reduced to the convergence $\sum_{g\in \mathrm{RM}(n/2-1,n)\setminus\{0\}} 2^{-\mathrm{wt}(g)}\to 0$. The solution explicitly does NOT prove this ("we do not reprove these Reed-Muller weight bounds here; they are the single external ingredient"). What is proved unconditionally is only that the minimum-weight term $2A_{w_0}2^{-w_0}\to0$ super-exponentially (Prop `prop:evenmin`). The solution itself stresses (e.g. $n=6$: tail $0.0422$ vs dominant $0.0795$) that $\sum_{w>w_0}A_w 2^{-w}$ is NOT $o(A_{w_0}2^{-w_0})$ for small $n$, so the dominant-term decay does not give the limit; the full-sum convergence is required and unproven. To close: state Kasami-Tokura precisely (weights in $[2^{n-k},2^{n-k+1})$ of $\mathrm{RM}(k,n)$ and their multiplicities); bound $\sum_{w_0\le w<2w_0}A_w2^{-w}$ explicitly; for $w\ge 2w_0$ use $A_w\le 2^M$ (or Sberlo-Shpilka/Samorodnitsky for the mid-range) and verify the whole sum is provably $o(1)$. As written this violates Commandments (1),(3): a load-bearing classical input is asserted, not applied with verified hypotheses.
